event: Coverage only; check tests for interrupt count regs.
Likely just reset/reg-access macros. Check for incr usage.
Only address maps. Check test C files for the counters.

I've submitted the verdict on finding f_8e312cf1f5e1 and it was accepted, so there's nothing left to run.

The finding stands as "untested" for most items. Only one test touches these counters: `mcu_intr_handler`, which fires events with software `INTR_TRIG` writes. It checks only that the summed hardware counts match a firmware count.

| Item | Outcome | Why |
|---|---|---|
| cr_ac50ef86787c (rising edge of the hardware event input) | verified | No test drives the hardware input. Only software triggers are used. |
| cr_b17476f90b95 (increment triggered by the hardware rising edge) | verified | Same gap as above. |
| cr_ad3bc76d7645 (increments by 1 per event) | withdrawn | The aggregate-sum check in `mcu_intr_handler` fails if the counts are off. It covers this indirectly. |
| cr_ad2b9f5593f2 (field is a counter) | inconclusive | Only implied by the counts matching, with no direct check. |
| cr_af3a97a3f2b9 (1-bit down-counter pulse) | inconclusive | Internal mechanism that no test checks directly. |

The test runs in the Nightly Directed and Strict regressions.
